page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g8a.16xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance built on the KVM hypervisor and powered by x86_64 AMD EPYC 9T24 processors operating at a base clock speed of 2.7 GHz. The instance configuration provides 64 dedicated vCPUs paired with 256 GB of system RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation of 4.0 GB per vCPU.

Network connectivity is defined by a 20 Gbps baseline bandwidth capacity. The server type contains no integrated local storage or hardware accelerators, requiring external network block storage volumes for persistent data operations and operating system files. Additionally, the instance is provisioned with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, utilizing standard virtual private cloud routing or assigned elastic addresses for public network communication.

With its high dedicated core count and standard memory density, the ecs.g8a.16xlarge instance balances compute capacity and memory footprint. This hardware profile suits parallel processing tasks that do not require local NVMe caching or GPU acceleration, including enterprise application backends, container orchestration nodes, multi-threaded CI/CD pipelines, and relational database tiers.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g8a.16xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine offering 64 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs and 256 GB of RAM, powered by AMD EPYC 9T24 processors running at 2.7 GHz on a KVM hypervisor. Featuring a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU, this instance targets compute and memory workloads requiring symmetrical resource allocation. Network performance is anchored by a 20 Gbps baseline bandwidth capacity. The instance includes no integrated local storage or GPU hardware, relying on external network block storage for persistence and OS volume management. It is also delivered without complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The ecs.g8a.16xlarge is engineered for enterprise-scale workloads such as microservices clusters, mid-tier web serving, continuous integration runners, relational databases, and data processing tasks requiring consistent multi-core performance across large parallel thread pools.
